findings.finding: Candidate #35 nulls showed no measured effect on the frozen potential/adaptation response surface, but recent activity-silent-memory work shows transient synaptic facilitation/state can preserve predictive information through periods of neural silence.
findings.impact: Keep #35 terminal and narrow. Do not generalize its negative result to all queue-free/activity-silent memory; any fresh broader successor should include a transient synaptic/STP carrier baseline.

sources: Gerstner et al. 2018, Front Neural Circuits 12:53, DOI 10.3389/fncir.2018.00053
findings.finding: Ordinary three-factor rules allow a delayed reward/third factor to act on a previously established eligibility trace. The current v0.5 path instead updates only when a new current pre/post pair enters apply(), so reward-only arrival does not consume the old trace.
findings.impact: Current v0.5 credit behavior is weaker than the standard delayed-credit baseline. Any future delayed-credit novelty claim must first implement or compare against reward/error acting on stored eligibility without a new qualifying spike pair.

sources: Bellec et al. 2020, Nature Communications 11:3625, DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-17236-y
findings.finding: e-prop separates synapse-local temporal eligibility from neuron/population-specific learning signals. Eligibility persistence and spatial responsibility assignment are distinct components of credit assignment.
findings.impact: Global scalar reward plus eligibility is an ordinary baseline and can solve limited distal reward through synaptic tags, but does not establish richer native causal-lineage responsibility. Future responsibility claims should compare against neuron/population-specific learning-signal baselines.

findings.finding: Modern local learning rules combine eligibility with explicit spatial credit signals, and 2026 three-factor rules jointly learn synaptic weights and transmission delays online.
findings.impact: Future SparkBrain locality/delayed-credit/learned-delay claims should use modern local forward and joint weight-delay three-factor baselines, not plain STDP as the strongest comparator.
